name: Prägraten am Großvenediger
kurzbeschreibung: Mountain village in the Virgental valley with views of the Großglockner – the perfect starting point for Nationalpark tours.
beschreibung:
Overview

Prägraten am Großvenediger is located at the majestic head of the Virgin Valley in the East Tyrolean district of Lienz at an elevation of 1,312 metres, nestled into the pristine core zone of the High Tauern National Park. This heritage-rich high-alpine municipality is home to approximately 1,140 permanent residents and spans an extensive territory of 180 square kilometres, framed to the north by the glaciated three-thousanders of the Venediger Group and to the south by the rugged Lasörling Group. The valley is crowned by the ancient majesty of Mount Großvenediger – at 3,657 metres the fourth-highest summit in Austria. The municipality comprises the historic hamlets of St. Andrä, Wallhorn, Bichl, Bobojach, Hinterbichl, and Ströden at the road's end. As an officially designated Mountaineering Village of the Alpine Convention, Prägraten is wholeheartedly committed to eco-friendly alpinism, mountain farming heritage, and pure alpine nature – free of ski lifts and hotel mega-resorts.

History

Prehistoric burials discovered in Hinterbichl dating from the 5th century BC bear witness to ancient copper extraction in the valley. Prägraten was first documented in written records in 1162 in property registers of Neustift Abbey near Brixen. For centuries, the locals sustained themselves in relative isolation through rugged alpine farming. The village made international mountaineering history on 3 September 1841 with the successful first ascent of Mount Großvenediger by an expedition led by Ignaz von Kürsinger and Josef Ranggetzer; from 1845 onwards, Hinterbichl became the primary southern trailhead for Venediger expeditions, giving birth to the renowned Virgin Valley mountain guide tradition. In 1857, the Johannishütte hut (2,121 m) was established in the Dorfertal valley, endowed by Archduke Johann – celebrated as the oldest alpine club hut in the Eastern Alps. The late Gothic Parish Church of St. Andrew, consecrated in 1516, anchors the village centre.

Getting There

Reaching Prägraten am Großvenediger is an inspiring journey through East Tyrol's high-alpine landscapes. Motorists arriving from Salzburg, Germany, or Kitzbühel take the Felbertauern Highway B108 to Matrei in Osttirol, turning onto the Virgin Valley road L24 through Virgen directly to Prägraten and the trailhead car park at Ströden; from the south, federal road B108 connects Lienz to Matrei. Rail passengers arrive at Lienz main station on the Drau Valley Railway. Connecting directly from Lienz station forecourt, VVT regional bus route 951 carries travellers without transfers through Matrei and Virgen straight to Prägraten, Hinterbichl, and Ströden. During summer, local Venediger hut taxi shuttles provide comfortable passenger transport to the trailhead of Johannishütte.

Tips

A natural marvel of continental renown is the Umbal Falls Water Experience Trail (Wasserschaupfad Umbalfälle): opened in 1976 as the very first educational water trail in Europe, dramatic cantilevered steel platforms jut out directly over the roaring glacial cascades and chasms of the Isel River, the last free-flowing glacier river in the Alps. For mountaineers, the guided glacier ascent of Mount Großvenediger (3,657 m) from Johannishütte via the Defereggerhaus hut is an essential alpine milestone. Long-distance trekkers relish the Venediger and Lasörling high trails connecting historic huts such as the Sajathütte and Clarahütte. In the valley, a stroll leads up to the Pilgrimage Church of St. Nicholas in Bichl, celebrated for its 16th-century frescoes, followed by authentic East Tyrolean delicacies such as handmade Schlipfkrapfen pasta.
